title: Summer warmth had uncertain links to the gap between leaf colour and leaf fall in eight Japanese tree samples in 1953-2020
abstract: We tested whether July-August warmth was linked to a longer gap between leaf colour and leaf fall. We used 5,743 paired records from JMA in 1953-2020. The common station set included ginkgo at 56 stations and maple at 50 stations. Eight models separated North and South Japan, two equal periods, and the two tree types. Models included station-by-observation-category and year effects, plus April-May and September temperature. Summer slopes ranged from -0.98 to +1.96 days per C. All marginal 95% intervals included zero. All intervals with an eight-test correction also included zero. Station trends, first differences and restricted observation samples did not give a common positive link. A next-year temperature diagnostic gave one positive link, which limits a causal interpretation. One diagnostic two-way variance was negative. We therefore report a consistent interval envelope using the largest of three cluster variances. Few northern stations, missing records, tree changes, coarse weather and late visible event definitions limit inference. The test does not measure the full senescence period, pollution or weather extremes. The package includes source tables, the derived panel, all models, figures, provenance, code and numerical checks.

display.caption: July-August temperature slopes for the gap between leaf colour and leaf fall. Thick lines show marginal 95% intervals. Thin lines show intervals with a correction for eight tests. All intervals include zero. All use the largest of three cluster variance estimates.

Summer-temperature slope estimates under nine model choices. Full intervals and sample sizes are preserved in estimates.csv. These checks did not show a common positive link. Colours are clipped at -2 and +2 days per C.
